claim: Buses #82 and #602 both leave Nice's Vauban station for Èze Village taking ~30 minutes, alternating roughly hourly, with #602 continuing to Monaco; avoid #600 which goes to Èze-sur-Mer instead.
quote: Two buses serve Eze Village: Bus #82 Plateau de la Justice and Bus #602 Monaco Casino. These alternate departures, so you'll have service approximately once hourly. Important: avoid Bus #600 Monaco, which goes to the seaside Eze-sur-Mer instead of the hilltop village.

claim: Lignes d'Azur tickets cost €1.70 with a rechargeable card or €4 from the driver; the #602 continues from Èze to Monaco in about 20 more minutes.
quote: A rechargeable Nice bus card costs €1.70 per journey... Buying directly from the driver costs €4 per ticket... Consider coordinating your return with Bus #602 to continue onward to Monaco (additional 20 minutes).

claim: Combining Èze in the morning with Monaco in the afternoon is the classic pairing because cruise passengers flood Monaco in the morning and clear out by afternoon.
quote: Visiting Eze in the morning allows you to avoid a crush of tourists; visiting Monaco in the afternoon means missing cruise ship passengers which discharge in the morning.

claim: Lignes d'Azur bus #15 from Nice runs through Villefranche-sur-Mer to the Passable/Rothschild stop right at Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild's entrance, making it the easiest single-vehicle route to Cap Ferrat.
quote: Line 15 connects 'Port de Saint Jean Cap Ferrat - Promenade des Arts'... The bus line goes through Villefranche-Sur-Mer - a picturesque fishing village... Arrival: Passable / Rothschild

claim: Villa Ephrussi plus a Cap Ferrat coastal walk fills a comfortable full day of roughly 7 hours including transit, with 2–3 hours for the villa and 2 more for the cape.
quote: You should be able to visit Villa Ephrussi and walk along the Cape quite easily in a day, with about two to three hours for the Villa and another two hours for a walk, comfortably doing it in around 7 hours including the bus ride.

claim: TER trains from Nice to Cannes via Antibes run ~16 times daily with direct fares from €6, taking about 20 minutes to Antibes and 30–45 to Cannes.
quote: Fares start at just $6 USD per way, the average direct train journey is 20 minutes, and there are approximately 16 trains leaving per day

claim: Antibes' Musée Picasso is housed in Château Grimaldi where Picasso worked in 1946, and the recommended sequence is Cannes/Lérins in the morning then Antibes' Picasso Museum after the tour-bus crowds leave.
quote: Pablo Picasso set up a studio at the city's Château Grimaldi, which now houses the Picasso Museum... The best sequence is Cannes and the island(s) in the morning/early afternoon. Then train back to Antibes... You will hit the Picasso Museum at the best time of day—after the bus tours have gone.

claim: Ferries to the Lérins Islands depart from Cannes' Quai Laubeuf for a 15-minute crossing; Sainte-Marguerite round-trip starts at €16 and Saint-Honorat is €20.50 online.
quote: Round trip ferry tickets from Cannes to Ste Marguerite Island start from €16... Ferry tickets to Île Saint Honorat are 20.5 euros online and 22 euros in person for a round trip... The trip takes about 15 minutes from Cannes

claim: The old #400 bus is gone; the current route is TER to Cagnes-sur-Mer (15 min, €3.80) then Zou bus #655 to the Saint-Paul Village stop (30 min, €2.10), totalling about an hour for €5.90 each way.
quote: Regional Express Train (TER) from Nice-Ville to Cagnes-sur-Mer (15 min, €3.80), then Zou bus 655 to Village stop in Saint-Paul de Vence (30 min, €2.10)... €5.90 per person one-way

claim: Fondation Maeght's bus stop is before the village so riders should alert the driver; a summer 'Maeght-Matisse' shuttle (1 July–30 Sept, Tue–Sat, 5x/day) links the foundation, Saint-Paul, and Matisse's Rosary Chapel in Vence.
quote: The bus stop for the Fondation Maeght is before Saint Paul. Make sure you tell the driver you intend to stop there... from 1st July to 30 Sept. there is a 'Maeght-Matisse' navette (shuttle bus), which runs from Tuesday to Saturday, 5 times a day.

claim: TER trains from Nice-Ville to Menton take about 40 minutes with returns around €11–13, and right-side seats face the sea.
quote: The train from Nice Ville to Menton takes just 40 minutes... Tickets were £13.75 return... Sit on the right-hand side of the train when leaving Nice for beautiful sea views

claim: Menton works as either a 3–4 hour half-day (Old Town plus Cocteau Museum) or a 6–8 hour full day adding Val Rahmeh botanical garden and Plage des Sablettes.
quote: half-day = Old Town + museum (~3–4 hours)... A complete day allows 6–8 hours to add beach time, gardens, or nearby villages like Roquebrune-Cap-Martin.

claim: Villefranche-sur-Mer (5–15 min by TER) is a half-day port village highlighted for its citadel, hidden 'Rue Obscure' street, and sandy beach.
quote: Villefranche-sur-Mer... Picturesque village, fortress, 'Rue Obscure' hidden street, sandy beach... Travel Time: 5-15 minutes... Duration: Half day
